CVE-2026-129481.title: Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown
CVE-2026-129481.description:
Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown.

The session extension records the filename of the executing script when a session starts. If a fatal error occurs in an application callback while the session variables are destroyed at shutdown, such as stream_close() of a user-defined stream wrapper, the pointer is retained after the request memory is freed, and a later request handled by the same worker can free the stale string. An attacker who can trigger such a failing cleanup may crash the worker or corrupt memory; code execution has not been demonstrated. This requires the filename to be allocated in request memory, for example when the script is not cached by OPcache.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: rtw88: usb: bound what the driver feeds the after-DTIM queue

Frames routed to the high queue are transmitted right after DTIM beacons
only, inside the ATIM window, while they wait in the shared TX page pool.
The driver puts no limit on how many it hands over, so as long as one
station dozes, any sustained broadcast or multicast traffic outruns the
drain and empties the pool: measured on an RTL8822BU AP with a single
client in power save and ~40 frames/s of mDNS chatter, the free page
count at 0x240 goes from 1803 to 16 in about 100 seconds and stays there
for as long as the traffic lasts. From that point every other transmit
queues behind the backlog, authentication responses arrive too late for
anyone to join, and the reserved page download fails ("error beacon
valid"). The AP keeps beaconing and only a reboot recovers.

Feed the high queue through a small budget that refills below the
measured drain rate…

CVE-2026-99692.title: ocfs2: stop recovery before shutting down local allocators
CVE-2026-99692.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: stop recovery before shutting down local allocators

Recovery completion needs the local allocators until it has finished
reclaiming a failed node's allocation window and truncate log. During
unmount, quota recovery is stopped first, but that leaves recovery_state
at OCFS2_REC_QUOTA_DISABLED. New non-quota recovery can still start.

ocfs2_truncate_log_shutdown() drains existing completion work and releases
osb_tl_bh before ocfs2_recovery_exit() closes that publication path:

Unmount Recovery
------- --------
stop quota recovery; disable quotas
truncate_log_shutdown()
flush existing completion work
recover another failed node
queue completion

CVE-2026-99726.title: drm/v3d: Widen cache_clean_lock over the whole L2TCACTL sequence
CVE-2026-99726.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/v3d: Widen cache_clean_lock over the whole L2TCACTL sequence

v3d_clean_caches() and v3d_flush_l2t() both write the single L2TCACTL
register and poll its status bits. The mutex cache_clean_lock exists to
serialize them, but v3d_clean_caches() only took the lock around its final
FLM_CLEAN write.

These functions run concurrently: v3d_flush_l2t() is issued from the
BIN/RENDER/CSD invalidate path while v3d_clean_caches() runs from the
CACHE_CLEAN queue, and each queue's scheduler uses its own ordered
workqueue, so their run_job callbacks execute in parallel.

Because clean locked only its final write, a concurrent flush can write
L2TCACTL during clean's unlocked phase. Both use non read-modify-write
writes to the one register, so whichever lands last wins: clean's TMUWCF
write can land on the flush's in-flight L2TFLS invalidate, triggering the
GFXH-1897 hazard of writing L2TCACTL while a flush is pending.

CVE-2026-99753.title: drm/loongson: Fix double free on BO initialization failure
CVE-2026-99753.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/loongson: Fix double free on BO initialization failure

If ttm_bo_init_validate() fails, it drops the buffer object's reference
and cleans it up through the supplied destroy callback. lsdc_bo_destroy()
releases the GEM object and frees the enclosing lsdc_bo, so freeing it
again in lsdc_bo_create() causes a double free on a synchronous failure
path.

Let TTM own the cleanup after initialization has started and return the
error directly. Keep the explicit free on drm_gem_object_init() failure,
which occurs before ownership is passed to TTM.

Tested on LS7A2000 by making drm_vma_offset_add() return -ENOSPC for one
selected dumb-buffer creation. The error reached userspace, the destroy
callback ran once, and no handle was published or tracked BO retained.
Normal buffer creation, zeroing, mapping, readback and release passed.
